package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a critical vulnerability (CVE-2017-9805) in version 2.5.12, which allows remote code execution (RCE) due to unsafe deserialization of attacker-controlled XML payloads by the XStreamHandler class. This vulnerability enables attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected systems by sending specially crafted XML to REST endpoints, posing a severe security risk.

execution_context.trigger: At runtime, when a REST endpoint implemented with struts2-rest-plugin receives and processes an XML payload from an HTTP request.
required_permissions: filesystem (for potential file writes during deserialization)
process execution (to allow arbitrary code execution if exploited)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: The createXStream method in XStreamHandler instantiates an XStream object without applying any type restrictions or input validation. When user-supplied XML is deserialized, arbitrary objects can be created and attacker-controlled code can be executed, leading to remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The method deserializes untrusted XML input directly using XStream without any type whitelisting, input validation, or sandboxing. This is a well-known anti-pattern that enables attackers to supply malicious XML that triggers instantiation of dangerous classes or execution of arbitrary code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Secure deserialization should enforce strict type whitelisting and validate all user input before processing. The actual implementation allows deserialization of any class referenced in the XML, violating the principle of least privilege and safe input handling.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Deserialization is legitimate when used with trusted, internal data sources and when XStream is configured to only allow specific, safe types. In secure applications, user input is never deserialized without validation.
key_indicators: Direct deserialization of user-supplied XML via XStream
Absence of type whitelisting or input validation in createXStream
XStreamHandler class present and used in REST endpoint processing
No security manager or sandboxing applied during deserialization

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends a specially crafted malicious XML payload to a REST endpoint implemented using the struts2-rest-plugin.
attack_chain.leads_to: The XML payload is received and passed to the XStreamHandler for processing.

attack_chain.action: The vulnerable createXStream method in XStreamHandler deserializes the attacker-supplied XML without any type restrictions or validation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Arbitrary objects are instantiated, potentially resulting in remote code execution on the server.

behavioral_signatures: Deserialization of XML payloads in REST endpoints using XStream without type restrictions
Invocation of XStreamHandler.createXStream on user-supplied XML data
Unexpected process execution, file writes, or network activity during XML deserialization
Application logs showing deserialization errors or exceptions in XStreamHandler
network_indicators: Inbound HTTP POST or PUT requests with XML content targeting REST endpoints
XML payloads containing references to unexpected or dangerous Java classes
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Scan application dependencies for the presence of struts2-rest-plugin version 2.5.12. Monitor application logs for deserialization errors or stack traces involving XStreamHandler. Use network IDS/IPS to detect inbound HTTP requests with suspicious XML payloads targeting REST endpoints, especially those containing references to classes outside expected application types. Employ runtime security monitoring to detect unexpected process execution or file system changes during XML deserialization. Consider blocking or alerting on the use of XStream without type whitelisting in REST endpoint code paths.
